structure: Part 9, Decisions ledger. Read in full: src/server/app/sets/high-risk-plants/spec/decisions.json (schema_version 1, one object with a decisions array of 84 entries d-001 to d-084; every entry has id, subject {kind conflict|behaviour, id}, ruling resolve|adopt|park, status, resolution, rationale, decidedBy panel|sam, decidedAt, dissent, supersedes, supersededBy, escalate) and src/server/app/sets/high-risk-plants/spec/panel/README.md (how the ledger works, the standing rulings of 2026-09-06, how to change a ruling). The ledger tallies: 40 resolve, 21 adopt, 23 park; 75 decided by panel, 9 by sam; every entry decidedAt 2026-09-06, status current, supersedes and supersededBy null, escalate false. Decisions fall into the panel's dockets: arrival and timing (d-001 to d-011), contact, consignor, origin error copy and declaration (d-012 to d-016), commodity model (d-017 to d-031), sources and who notifies (d-032 to d-040), out-of-scope internal and platform behaviours (d-041 to d-048), formats, labels and origin lists (d-049 to d-059), reference, status and post-submission actions (d-060 to d-066), chrome, dashboard, hub and guidance (d-067 to d-073), non-functional requirements and MI (d-074 to d-083) and the copy tripwires (d-084). Claims below take each decision in ledger order: what it rules, quoted by id and words, with who decided where it was Sam and the losing dissent where one is recorded. The panel's evidence files (rulings.json, critic.json) are out of scope and were not read.

claims.statement: The plants set keeps one rulings ledger, spec/decisions.json, with one entry per ruling stamped onto its subject (a conflict's resolution and decision, or a behaviour's status and decision); it is the only place a ruling lives, and conflicts and behaviours carry only a pointer to it.
claims.quote: `../decisions.json` is the ledger: one entry per ruling, stamped onto its subject (a conflict's `resolution` and `decision`, or a behaviour's `status` and `decision`). It is the only place a ruling lives; conflicts.json and the behaviours carry a pointer to it, never their own answer.

claims.statement: The ledger's rulings came from a judges panel: eight dockets, three judges and a chair each, with one ruling per item decided by the panel, or by Sam where a standing product-owner ruling settled it.
claims.quote: eight dockets, three judges and a chair each, one ruling per item with rationale, spec changes, dissent and who decided it (`panel`, or `sam` where a standing product-owner ruling settled it).

claims.statement: Standing ruling for the first pass (2026-09-06): users, sign-in models, agents, delegation of authority, plant-operator registration and 'who notifies' are out of phase, parked rather than rejected.
claims.quote: Standing rulings for the first pass (2026-09-06): users, sign-in models, agents, delegation of authority, plant-operator registration and "who notifies" are out of phase; bulk upload is out of phase. Both are parked, not rejected.

claims.statement: Standing ruling for the first pass (2026-09-06): bulk upload is out of phase, parked rather than rejected.
claims.quote: bulk upload is out of phase. Both are parked, not rejected.

claims.statement: A ruling is never changed by editing the ledger or evidence files: a new decision is added with tools/journey-builder/spec-add-decision.sh naming the decision it supersedes, which marks the earlier entry superseded and re-stamps the subject.
claims.quote: To change a ruling, do not edit any of these files. From the workspace: ... tools/journey-builder/spec-add-decision.sh EUDPA-409 --subject conflict:c-012 ... --supersedes d-0NN ... The earlier entry is marked superseded and the subject is re-stamped.

claims.statement: All 84 ledger decisions are current, all were decided on 2026-09-06, none supersedes or is superseded by another and none is escalated; 75 were decided by the panel and 9 by Sam (d-033, d-034, d-035, d-036, d-039, d-040, d-077, d-083, d-084).
claims.ref: src/server/app/sets/high-risk-plants/spec/decisions.json (every entry: status, decidedAt, supersedes, supersededBy, escalate, decidedBy)
claims.quote: "status": "current" ... "decidedAt": "2026-09-06" ... "supersedes": null ... "supersededBy": null ... "escalate": false
claims.note: Counted with jq over the whole decisions array: 40 resolve, 21 adopt, 23 park.

claims.statement: d-001 (conflict c-001): 'Great Britain', never England, appears in every notifier-facing string (arrival-status heading and legend, arrival date labels, place-of-landing hint, confirmation body).
claims.quote: d-001: 'Great Britain' wins in every notifier-facing string (arrival-status heading and legend, arrivalDate labels by state, proposedPlaceOfLanding hint, confirmation body; the dashboard intro names no territory today — guidance-before-you-start)

claims.statement: d-001: the service applies no nation or territory check to the place-of-destination address, so a Scottish or Welsh destination is notified through this service; the SI's England-only drafting is a legal note, not rendered and not built.
claims.quote: d-001: the service applies no nation or territory check to the placeOfDestination address, so a Scottish or Welsh destination is notified through this service. The SI's England-only drafting is recorded as a legal note on the england-vs-great-britain behaviour, not rendered and not built.

claims.statement: d-002 (c-002): one arrival date is collected for every commodity type; arrival time only for potatoes; arrival status only for plants for planting and wood and cut trees.
claims.quote: d-002: Collect exactly the statutory matters: one arrivalDate for every commodity type; arrivalTime only when commodityType = potatoes; arrivalStatus only for plants-for-planting and wood-and-cut-trees.

claims.statement: d-002: a potato notification is always pre-arrival ('Expected date of arrival'); a past date is accepted and flagged late, never rejected; no actual-arrival date or time is added for potatoes, and the arrival-status page is hidden for potatoes by the derived gate (no authored gate).
claims.quote: d-002: A potato notification is always framed as pre-arrival ('Expected date of arrival'), a past date is accepted and flagged late by lateNotificationIndicator, never rejected, and no actual-arrival date or time is added for potatoes; the arrival-status page needs no authored gate because the derived gate hides it for potatoes.

claims.statement: d-002 rationale: the label 'Expected date of arrival' shown for potatoes that have already arrived is resolved by a hint line rather than a new question.
claims.quote: d-002: The one service-design gap is the label 'Expected date of arrival' shown to somebody whose potatoes arrived yesterday: a hint line resolves it without a new matter.

claims.statement: d-003 (c-006) and d-008: the importer selects arrival status on its own single-question radios page (plants and wood only, Yes first), placed before arrival details and place of destination; the service never derives the status from the date.
claims.quote: d-003: The importer selects arrivalStatus on its own single-question page (plants and wood only, radios Yes first) before arrival-details and place-of-destination; the service never derives it from the date.

claims.statement: d-003: the place-of-destination page's already-arrived copy tells a notifier whose consignment has landed but not yet reached its destination to give the intended destination.
claims.quote: d-003: the destination page's already-arrived copy tells a notifier whose consignment has landed but not reached its destination to give the intended destination, so one binary status serves both clauses.

claims.statement: d-004 (c-029) and d-010: the arrival date validates as a real calendar date with no sanity window and no animals-style bounds.
claims.quote: d-004: arrivalDate validates as a real calendar date (dateText) with no sanity window and no animals-style bounds

claims.statement: d-004: when arrival status is already-arrived the arrival date may not be after today in Europe/London (max only), and the date picker carries a max date only in that state and never a min date.
claims.quote: d-004: when arrivalStatus = already-arrived the date may not be after today in Europe/London (dateTextInRange, max only) because it is 'the date on which it first arrived' — and the picker carries data-max-date only in that state and no data-min-date in any state.

claims.statement: d-004: expected dates (potatoes, not yet arrived) accept any past or future date; lateness is computed, never validated; a typo sanity window is parked. The GDS judge's one-year-each-way window lost.
claims.quote: d-004: Expected dates (potatoes, not-yet-arrived) accept any past or future date; lateness is computed, never validated; a typo sanity window is parked, not built.

claims.statement: d-005 (c-031): plants and wood may be notified before arrival or no later than four days after the date of arrival; potatoes only before, at least two days before the expected date.
claims.quote: d-005: The SI wording wins: plants and wood may be notified before arrival or no later than four days after the date of arrival; potatoes only before, at least two days before the expected date.

claims.statement: d-005: lateness is calendar-day arithmetic in Europe/London ignoring arrival time: potatoes are late when notified after arrival date minus 2 days, plants and wood when after arrival date plus 4 days; notifying on the boundary day is on time; a future date can be late for potatoes but never for plants and wood.
claims.quote: d-005: Lateness is calendar-day arithmetic in Europe/London and ignores arrivalTime — potatoes are late when the notification day is after arrivalDate minus 2 days, plants and wood when it is after arrivalDate plus 4 days (notifying on arrivalDate minus 2, or on arrivalDate plus 4, is on time); a future date can still be late for potatoes but never for plants and wood

claims.statement: d-005: the timing windows are shown up front as option hints on the commodity-type page and per state on the arrival-status page.
claims.quote: d-005: the windows are shown up front as option hints on commodity-type and per state on arrival-status.

claims.quote: d-006: After submission the late highlight is shown in three places — a govukNotificationBanner naming the rule breached on the confirmation page and on the SUBMITTED read-only check-your-answers view, and a Late tag beside the status on the dashboard card

claims.statement: d-006: before submission the draft check-your-answers page shows warning text when the entered date would make the notification late if submitted today, and says it can still be submitted; lateness never blocks and there is no separate late page.

It never blocks and there is no separate late page.
claims.note: The policy judge's dissent to park the pre-submission warning lost 2-1.

claims.statement: d-006 and d-007: lateNotificationIndicator is a system-populated obligation computed by one pure helper from (clock, commodityType, arrivalDate) and stored at the declaration POST immediately before submit only when the journey is DRAFT; confirmation, the submitted check-your-answers view and the dashboard Late tag read the stored value and never recompute.
claims.quote: d-006: lateNotificationIndicator is a manifest obligation with system: true, listed in SYSTEM_POPULATED ... whose result is committed as a system value in fulfilment immediately before submitJourney only when the journey is DRAFT (c-030); confirmation, the submitted check-your-answers view and the dashboard Late tag read the stored value and never recompute from submittedAt.

claims.quote: d-007: Build it in the first pass as a stored system value ... leaving it untouched on a re-submit from AMEND (c-030) ... No finalise hook, no backend field, no engine change.

claims.quote: d-009: The residual legal question — whether the draft SI is widened to GB or Scottish and Welsh instruments mirror it, and whether a Scottish or Welsh destination ever routes elsewhere — is recorded as PARKED (policy) inside this behaviour and changes no page.

claims.quote: d-011: routing, access parity and region derivation from the address are revisited when the plants backend has typed fields or an outbox.

claims.quote: d-015: Keep the animals id, page, widget, validation, label, hint and Welsh label and hint verbatim; change only the error sentence to 'Select the country where the consignment originates from'

claims.quote: d-016: Keep the declaration page and its machinery exactly as animals has them — the single checkbox, its confirmation sentence in English and Welsh, the error copy, the date line, Continue, the flow-only key and submit gate.

claims.statement: d-016: none of the five animals declaration statements survives; the plants declaration carries three provisional statements: the submission is the written notification under the Plant Health National Notification Scheme; the relevant authority (APHA, the Forestry Commission or Scottish Government) may spot-check without prior notice at the destination or where the consignment is currently held; failing to notify, notifying late or giving incorrect details may be treated as a non-compliance.
claims.quote: d-016: Replace the five animals statements wholesale: none survives. The first pass carries three short plants statements grounded in the policy paper — (1) this submission is the written notification to the competent authority under the Plant Health National Notification Scheme; (2) the relevant plant health authority (APHA, the Forestry Commission or Scottish Government) may spot-check the consignment without prior notice at its place of destination or where it is currently held; (3) failing to notify, notifying late or giving incorrect details may be treated as a non-compliance — flagged provisional copy for policy and content-design sign-off, with no Welsh invented.

claims.quote: d-016: The third-party / agent-authority clauses are parked with agent-acting-on-behalf under standing ruling 2, not written ... The sub-park of the third-party and agent-authority clauses is decidedBy sam (standing ruling 2).

claims.quote: d-017: Seed potatoes are potatoes: commodityType = potatoes, the per-line category offers seed-potatoes and ware-potatoes, and a seed-potato line takes the reg 24A matters (variety, quantity, intended use, producer and crop ids, time of arrival, place of landing) and the two-day pre-arrival window. ... claims.quote: d-019: The preservative exclusion moves from the treatments hint to a hint on the category question shown for wood notifications, worded with its cut-coniferous-trees exception.

claims.quote: d-021: The hardwood genus constraint is Castanea, Fraxinus and Platanus only. Juglans and Pterocarya are not offered anywhere in the service

claims.quote: d-022: All lines share the one commodityType chosen first; a consignment mixing potatoes with plants or wood is two notifications.
